title: From Statutory Reporting to Africa Empowerment: Launch Workshop for National Focal Points of the Fourth Cycle of Periodic Reporting in Africa
content: The Launch Workshop for National Focal Points marked the official commencement of the Fourth Cycle of Periodic Reporting in Africa under the 1972 World Heritage Convention. UNESCO and the Government of Uganda, through the Ministry of Tourism, Wildlife and Antiquities, co-organised the workshop in close collaboration with the African World Heritage Fund (AWHF). title: Putting human rights at the heart of World Heritage protection
content: Paris, 9 November 2026 – Protecting the world's natural and cultural heritage cannot be separated from respecting the human rights of the people and communities connected to it. title: New ICMM dataset contributes to greater transparency on mining and biodiversity
content: The International Council on Mining and Metals (ICMM) has published a new global dataset and report examining the spatial relationship between mining and metals facilities and areas of biodiversity and conservation importance. title: Post-Earthquake Recovery of Cultural Heritage in Myanmar
content:
Empowering local communities to take the first step towards the recovery of Myanmar's earthquake-damaged cultural heritage.
Background
Following the 28 March 2025 earthquakes in central Myanmar, extensive damage was reported across Mandalay Region, Sagaing Region, and southern Shan State, including cultural heritage sites associated with the 'Ancient cities of Upper Myanmar: Innwa, Amarapura, Sagaing, Mingun, Mandalay' on the World Heritage Tentative List.

title: Researcher Sanjay Saifi (India) Awarded the 2026 World Heritage Decorated Farmhouses of Hälsingland International Scholarship
content:
The Culture and Competence Committee of Region Gävleborg has decided to award the  World Heritage Scholarship 2026 to researcher Sanjay Saifi for his research project, "Timber Against Time: Climate-Resilient Wooden Heritage in Sweden and Japan.”

title: UNESCO strengthens sustainable tourism management at Fuerte de Samaipata
content:
UNESCO Montevideo organized a training workshop in Samaipata, Bolivia, on tourism carrying capacity at the Fuerte de Samaipata World Heritage property.
The initiative aimed to strengthen management tools to ensure the conservation of the property in the face of increasing visitor numbers, contributing to more sustainable tourism management of cultural heritage.

title: UNESCO–Africa–China Workshop strengthens World Heritage capacity and cooperation in Quanzhou
content:
The UNESCO-Africa-China Workshop on World Heritage, Capacity-Building and Cooperation brought together 26 heritage professionals from 17 African countries in Quanzhou, China, from 20 to 25 October 2026. Through six days of exchanges and practical training with Chinese experts and international partners, participants explored how to strengthen World Heritage nominations, conservation, monitoring and management of cultural and natural heritage.

title: COP17: New assessment highlights World Heritage Convention's contribution to global biodiversity goals
content:
A new technical note published by the IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas (WCPA), in partnership with the UNESCO World Heritage Centre, examines how the World Heritage Convention is reflected in national efforts to implement the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF). It also identifies opportunities to further strengthen its contribution to global biodiversity goals.

title: Climate Action Toolkit for World Heritage tested in the Colonial City of Santo Domingo
content:
The Colonial City of Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic is hosting the first pilot application of the Climate Action Toolkit at a cultural site, and the first in Latin America and the Caribbean. The pilot, taking place from September to November 2026, combines online sessions with an in-person workshop held from 5 to 9 October.

title: The Asia-Pacific Dialogue on Heritage and Authenticity brings new perspectives to World Heritage preservation
content: From 27 September to 1 October 2026, a Dialogue on Heritage and Authenticity for the Asia-Pacific region took place in Ha Noi and Ninh Binh (Viet Nam).
